title: Rights-Request Engine for Rejected Applicants
one_liner: A consumer tool that files legally formatted data-access and automated-decision requests to employers' hiring systems, turning silent rejections into scores, reasons and evidence.
customer: Job seekers, starting in the UK and EU under GDPR Art. 15/22, then Illinois and California. They pay $12 a month or $29 per request pack. Secondary buyers are plaintiff-side employment firms and researchers who license opt-in aggregate data.
problem: Applicants send dozens of applications, get almost no replies and never learn why (HN: 65 applications, 3 phone screens, 0 interviews). New laws give people rights to see and contest automated screening, but nobody uses them because finding the right contact and format is a hassle.
solution: A browser extension logs each application (company, ATS vendor, date). After 30 days of silence it files a data-access and automated-decision request, tracks the one-month deadline, escalates to the regulator, and parses the response into a structured 'why I was screened out' report. Opt-in aggregate stats show which employers and ATS vendors auto-reject which profiles.
why_now: California's automated-decision regulations start binding in Jan 2027 and Illinois' AI-in-employment notice law took effect Jan 2026. The Mobley v. Workday collective action is live and AI resume screening is ubiquitous. Job-search desperation is at a peak, and EU/UK rights already work today.
revenue_model: Consumer subscription or per-pack fees, plus opt-in anonymised data and insight licences to labor economists, unions and employment plaintiff firms. Employer-side compliance-readiness upsell later.
non_obvious_insight: Regulators created rights but no practical channel, and that friction is the enforcement gap. The service converts individual rights into aggregate leverage: an employer receiving 500 requests per role starts giving candidates real feedback, and the request-and-response dataset becomes the moat.
first_30_days: Build a GDPR-only MVP (templates, deadline tracker) for UK/EU applicants in two weeks, with a UK data-protection solicitor reviewing the templates. Seed it in UK and EU job-search communities and HN at £9 per pack. Measure response rates and refine.

title: Orphan-Element Audits for Copper Concentrate and Tailings
one_liner: A 90-day survey that measures the tellurium, selenium, bismuth, cobalt, germanium, rhenium, indium and scandium copper mines already ship for free, then brokers by-product credit rights with refiners.
customer: Mid-size copper miners (Arizona, Utah, Nevada, Chile, Peru, Zambia, Kazakhstan) who sell concentrate to smelters or run SX-EW, paying $40-120k per site survey. Refiners and specialty-metal buyers (Aurubis-type smelters, Umicore, 5N Plus-type processors) pay finder fees. Government programmes such as DoD DPA Title III and DLA support recovery projects.
problem: Smelter contracts pay for Cu, Au and Ag. Te, Se, Bi, Co, Ge, In, Sb and Re are either given away, or shown only as penalty elements (As, Sb, Bi, Hg, F). The plant lab measures the penalty elements and stops. The 48-element ICP-MS suite exists only on exploration drill core from ten years ago and never on the concentrate, tailings, SX raffinate or electrolyte bleed streams. The smelter quietly captures value in anode slimes and flue dust. The miner has no data to negotiate with. Meanwhile, benchmark treatment charges for 2026 reportedly collapsed to around zero, so smelters are squeezed and newly hunting for by-product margin and for clean feed. Chinese export controls on Te, Bi, In, Ga, Ge, Sb and others make Western buyers desperate.
solution: A productised survey: pull 30-60 retained samples from process streams (every mine keeps monthly composite retains), run multi-element ICP-MS plus automated mineralogy through partner labs, and deliver an 'orphan-element balance' showing tonnes per year and contained value per element. Then hand the mine a negotiation kit: by-product participation clauses for offtake contracts, dust and slime credit language, and penalty-threshold renegotiation. Route the data to refiners and toll processors who can recover the element. The compensation is a survey fee plus 10-20% of by-product margin for 5 years, or a finder fee at contract signing.
why_now: In 2025 China imposed export controls on tellurium, bismuth, indium, gallium, germanium and antimony, with rare earths restrictions following. US and EU strategic stockpile, offtake and grant programmes now pay for domestic by-product supply. Smelters are under profit pressure from near-zero treatment charges and are open to sharing upside with suppliers. Prices for Te and Bi jumped.
revenue_model: $40-120k per site survey, plus a 10-20% by-product royalty or finder fee on recovered element revenue, plus a refiner-side subscription for a pipeline of quantified feed.
non_obvious_insight: The barrier is not technology. Kennecott has produced tellurium for decades. It is that nobody measured, so nobody owns the value, and contracts were signed when no one cared. The person who knows how the process streams flow (where it goes to anode slimes, where to dust) can tell which stream concentrates each element.
first_30_days: Ask ten friendly mid-tier mines for retained composite samples, or buy access to public tailings and concentrate assays. Run 15 multi-element packs at $60-150 each (about $2k in total). Produce a one-page 'value at stake' per mine and email it to 30 operations and commercial managers. Sell 2-3 pilot surveys at $25k. Meanwhile call two refiners and one federal programme office with the resulting map to line up demand.

title: Youth-Slang Drift API for Safety Teams
one_liner: A continuously updated, human-verified lexicon and drift detector for Gen Alpha and teen slang, coded risk terms and grooming language, sold as an API to moderation and school-safety teams.
customer: Trust-and-safety teams at game and social platforms, K-12 student-monitoring vendors, school-safety directors, and moderation stacks inside AI toys and companions.
problem: Youth language shifts every few months. Classifiers trained on last year's data misread banter and miss coded terms for sextortion, self-harm and grooming. School monitors bury counselors in false alerts. As bans push kids into private chats and games, moderation teams are older and further from the language.
solution: A lexicon with context tags (benign, hazard, coded-risk; severity; platform of origin; age range), plus alerts when a term's usage or meaning shifts, delivered via API and a weekly briefing. It is built with a paid panel of consented 16-19-year-old language scouts (parental consent where needed) and linguists.
why_now: Age-gated platform tiers, bans and duty-of-care laws raise the cost of missed threats. Moderation is now LLM-based and needs fresh context that models lack. Volume and speed of Gen Alpha slang keep growing.
revenue_model: $2-15k a month per platform or vendor for API and briefings, plus custom lexicon builds.
non_obvious_insight: LLMs know last year's slang, so freshness is a data-supply problem. The moat is the paid youth panel and labeling process, not the model.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 teens (with parental consent) and 3 linguists. Publish a free monthly 'Gen Alpha threat lexicon' for trust-and-safety newsletters. Land 2 design partners, one school-monitoring vendor and one kids' game, at $1k a month each.

title: Retiree Remote-Assist Bench for Robot Fleets
angle: Pairing 1: Aging/silver economy x Logistics & physical automation
one_liner: A certified, US-based, part-time pool of retirees (ex-truckers, dispatchers, yard hands) who resolve robot and AV exceptions, billed by the assisted hour to fleet operators.
customer: Operators of driverless trucks, yard-automation systems, delivery robots and warehouse fleets (Bot Auto, Gatik, YardFlow-style deployments, sidewalk-robot firms), paying $45-65 per assisted hour.
problem: Every fleet needs remote humans for edge cases. Waymo alone runs about 70 agents on shift, partly in the Philippines, and offshore assist is now a political and first-responder question (NHTSA letter, Jul 2026). Meanwhile 65+ workers want flexible seated income and have the domain judgment, for example reading a truck yard or a weigh station.
solution: Recruit and train retirees on a common exception-handling curriculum. Certify them per vehicle or robot type. Supply them as a managed bench with scheduling, QA and a US-based, background-checked compliance story. Retirees earn $28-40 an hour for 10-20 hours a week, which keeps them under Social Security earnings limits.
why_now: Driverless freight went early-commercial in 2026 (Aurora about 200 trucks, Gatik 85k orders). Fleets are scaling remote-assist headcount, and regulators are scrutinizing where it sits.
revenue_model: Managed-service margin: bill $45-65 per hour, pay $28-40, keep about 35% gross margin. Add training and certification fees per operator.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input for autonomy is not more compute. It is cheap, trustworthy human judgment on demand. The demographic everyone treats as a care burden is the best-matched supply of that judgment.
first_30_days: Pitch two mid-size operators for a paid pilot in one metro (freight yards, sidewalk robots). Recruit 25 retired CDL drivers and dispatchers via trucker associations and AARP groups. Run a two-week training and bill the pilot at cost-plus.

title: Good-Better-Best Estimate Engine for Vet Clinics
one_liner: AI scribes are turning into a free feature, so the money moves to the moment a client sees the estimate: automate tiered spectrum-of-care plans that turn declines into partial acceptance.
customer: Emergency/urgent-care hospitals and 2-10 DVM independent general practices, where estimates over $1,000 are routine. Buyer is the practice owner or hospital manager.
problem: Per the briefing, 85% of vet professionals say clients decline care at estimates of $1,000 or less, and 86% alter treatment plans weekly for financial reasons. Estimates are still hand-built as one gold-standard plan, so declines are lost revenue and a source of moral distress (33% of vets find below-gold care distressing). Nobody logs why clients decline.
solution: Reads the diagnosis or SOAP note from any scribe or PIMS and drafts three clinician-approved tiers: full workup, stabilize-and-monitor, and essential/palliative. Each tier is priced from the clinic's own fee schedule, with consent language, expected-outcome ranges and stage-gated steps (approve step 1 now, decide step 2 after results). Financing and insurance pre-check sit on the same screen. Every decline reason is captured and feeds a protocol library written with boarded clinicians. Ships as a browser overlay on the PIMS estimate screen.
why_now: IDEXX bought the CoVet AI scribe on 2026-09-16 and says it will stay compatible with non-IDEXX systems. That marks documentation AI as a bundled strategic feature and squeezes standalone scribes. Clinic visits have reportedly fallen three years running, and price, not demand, is the constraint.
revenue_model: SaaS at $300-600 per clinic per month, plus an optional success fee of 3-5% of incremental accepted revenue measured against a pre-pilot baseline. Later, anonymized decline-reason data sold to insurers and lenders.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders think the AI prize is saving doctors' time on notes. The budget line is revenue at the decision moment, and the scribe is just a commodity input to it. The decline reason is a dataset nobody collects, and it is what financiers and insurers most want.
first_30_days: Sign 5 ER/urgent-care sites and 5 independents. Take each site's last 20 de-identified declined estimates, have a contract boarded vet rebuild them as three-tier plans, and run a 4-week pilot tracking acceptance rate. Charge a $1,500 pilot fee. Prototype the browser overlay with an LLM plus the clinic's fee-schedule export.

title: Co-op Ledger Signals: Farm Distress Early Warning
one_liner: Benchmark co-ops on their own receivables, then sell the anonymized, county-level 'who is paying whom first' data to lenders, insurers and equipment financiers as a leading indicator of farm distress.
customer: First payers: co-op managers and CFOs, who buy the benchmark dashboard. Data buyers: Farmer Mac, Farm Credit institutions, regional ag banks, equipment captive finance arms, input manufacturers, ag reinsurers and funds trading farm-exposed equities.
problem: Ag bank delinquency stats and Fed surveys lag reality by two to three quarters. Meanwhile every co-op ERP quietly holds the earliest signal: accounts-receivable aging by customer, the timing of input payments, and who is asking for deferred-payment or extended-terms deals. Farmers in trouble pay in a predictable order (operating lender, landlord, seed, then the co-op), so slow co-op payments show up long before defaults. Each co-op sees only its own trade area and cannot tell whether its collection problems are local or systemic.
solution: Ship a free-to-cheap benchmark: connect the co-op's grain and ag-retail accounting system (Agvance, Agris and similar) and get peer comparisons on A/R over 90 days, prepay behavior, and credit-line usage. In return, contribute anonymized data to a pooled index with strict privacy rules (a minimum of 5 co-ops per cell, county-by-month, no farmer-level data). Sell the county-level Farm Payment Stress Index to lenders and funds, with a second SKU for weekly harvest-pace and grain-quality metrics (moisture, test weight, damage) from scale tickets. Co-ops receive a revenue share.
why_now: Chapter 12 filings are up sharply, the Chicago Fed reports rising loan rollovers and falling cash rents, and USDA projects record farm debt. Federal data proved brittle during the fall 2025 shutdown, and lenders and funds want independent ground truth without waiting for quarterly surveys.
revenue_model: Co-op benchmark subscription ($300 to $800 a month). Index licenses to lenders and reinsurers ($25k to $150k a year). Fund data feeds ($5k to $15k a month). Co-ops receive 40% to 50% of data revenue.
non_obvious_insight: The co-op's boring back-office ledger is the best real-time farm-distress sensor in America. Co-op managers think the data is too mundane to sell. The way to get it is to give them the peer benchmark they have always wanted and only then aggregate.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 to 8 co-ops through state co-op councils and CFO peer groups with a free 'A/R health check'. Build an ETL for the two or three most common co-op ERPs. Produce the first county-level index by Q4 2026. Pitch two ag lenders and one reinsurer for paid pilots.

title: Twelve-Week Friend Pods, Paid by Cafes
one_liner: Fixed cohorts of six adults meet weekly at the same cafe for 12 weeks, backed by a refundable attendance deposit, with the venue paying for guaranteed slow-hour covers.
customer: Two payers. Adults 25-45 who moved cities or lost their friend group ($75 refundable deposit plus about $25 a month). Independent cafes, bars and climbing gyms paying roughly $8-12 per seat-night for guaranteed off-peak traffic.
problem: Friend-making products optimize the first meeting, and one-off stranger dinners rarely convert. Research on friendship formation (Hall, 2018) puts casual friendship at roughly 50 hours together and real friendship at about 90. Meanwhile 24% of US adults with only a high-school education report zero close friends (up from 3% in 1990). Every app's economics reward churn, not durable friendship.
solution: Pods of 6 matched by neighborhood and schedule, not personality. 12 weekly 2.5-hour sessions at one partner venue, with a trained host for the first four weeks who then fades out. The deposit is refunded per session attended. After week 12 the pod 'graduates' into a standing-table subscription. Hosts earn a bonus tied to the share of pod members still meeting at week 20.
why_now: Bumble cut 30% of staff (Jun 2025) and relaunched BFF around groups (Sep 2025), which shows demand for friend-making but not retention. Run clubs proved people pay for recurring in-person belonging. Independent venues face weak weekday traffic and want guaranteed covers.
revenue_model: Membership of about $25 a month per member, forfeited deposits (typically 10-15%), and a per-seat-night fee from venues. Host bonuses are the main cost. Scales city by city with a lean local ops lead.
non_obvious_insight: Friendship is a dose problem, not a matching problem. Every product is paid at the moment of the first meeting, so all of them optimize matches. The only metric worth charging on is hours-together at week 20. Venues, not users, are the natural payer for attendance, because a seated pod is guaranteed revenue on a dead Tuesday.
first_30_days: Pick one neighborhood. Sign 6 cafes with dead Tuesday-Thursday slots on a flat per-seat guarantee. Recruit 4 pods (24 people) through local run-club and Instagram audiences and collect the $75 deposits up front (about $1,800 of first cash). Hire 2 part-time hosts and start week 1 in month 2. Track attendance at weeks 6 and 12.

title: Tariff Refund Recovery for Downstream Buyers
one_liner: Importers of record are collecting over $100B in tariff refunds, but the small businesses that paid tariff surcharges on their invoices are owed a share and nobody is collecting it for them.
customer: Mid-size US contractors, restaurant groups, retailers and manufacturers ($5M-$200M revenue) whose 2025-26 supplier invoices carried explicit tariff surcharges or tariff-attributed price increases.
problem: Refunds go to the importer of record, and many importers already passed the cost through. Downstream buyers may have contract or unjust-enrichment claims, but their AP teams never tracked surcharges. Small importers also find filing costly ('not without a cost,' Colorado Sun, 2026-07-02), so cash sits with parties who have no incentive to share it.
solution: Connect to QuickBooks, NetSuite or the AP inbox and extract every invoice line mentioning a tariff or surcharge. Map each vendor to its importer of record using public import records. Estimate the refund-attributable share and generate demand packets with contract citations. A partner law firm handles escalations on contingency. Default settlement is a vendor credit memo, which preserves the relationship.
why_now: More than $100B has been refunded (CNBC 2026-08-07, Forbes 2026-09-09), the government is fighting an order to refund all importers (WaPo 2026-08-11), tariff lawsuits are surging, and 25 states are challenging the replacement Section 122 tariffs. That means a second wave of surcharges to track.
revenue_model: 20-30% contingency on recovered cash or credits. After the first recovery, $299-$999 per month SaaS to track surcharges and refund clauses on future tariff swings.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is watching who receives the refund, and nobody watches who funded it. Many invoices literally say 'tariff surcharge, pass-through.' Vendors prefer credit memos to cash, so recoveries can be quiet and relationship-safe. The same invoice-clause tooling becomes a permanent tariff-swing shield.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 SMBs through trade associations and small-business communities and pull 24 months of AP exports. Run the analysis by hand with a lawyer's template letter and produce a $1M aggregate identified-claim demo. Sign two contingent agreements and send the first ten demand letters.

title: Trust-Fund Compliance for Family Vloggers
one_liner: A minutes-on-screen tracker and escrow tool that computes, sets aside and documents the trust share owed to kids who appear in monetized family channels.
customer: Family channel operators on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram earning $50k+ a year, influencer agencies and MCNs, and brands and payment processors that want a 'clean hands' certificate.
problem: Several states have passed laws on minors in monetized content: Illinois (2024) requires a trust share by on-screen time, Minnesota (2025) restricts under-14 content creation for pay, and California extended Coogan-style protections (details from memory). Parents compute set-asides by hand. Brands and platforms are exposed, and grown kids and documentaries are fueling backlash.
solution: The tool ingests channel data, uses vision models to measure each child's on-screen minutes per video, computes the state-specific set-aside, generates records and moves funds into a custodial trust, UTMA or custodial investment account. It also keeps consent and deletion logs and issues brand-facing compliance certificates.
why_now: The state laws took effect in 2024-25, public scrutiny of family-vlogging is at a high, and a new custodial-account channel (Trump Accounts, opened July 2026, per the brief) gives set-asides a natural home.
revenue_model: $99-499 a month per channel or about 1% of earnings, plus per-campaign brand compliance certificates.
non_obvious_insight: The real buyers are brands and platforms that need a clean-hands certificate, and creators who need to avoid legal exposure. It works like marketplace sales-tax automation, and the child is the beneficiary, not the customer.
first_30_days: Ship a free on-screen-minutes calculator. DM 100 family channels with 50k-2M subscribers. Sell a $299 compliance setup with an attorney-reviewed template. Approach 3 influencer agencies for a group deal.

title: Chain-of-Custody Certificates for Spent PFAS Media
one_liner: A broker and tracking service that consolidates spent GAC and ion-exchange media from small utilities, routes it to verified destruction, and issues auditable certificates that document where the waste went.
customer: Small and mid-size water systems that have installed or are installing PFAS treatment, plus the treatment vendors and engineers who can bundle the service. Utilities pay per ton, and vendors pay referral fees.
problem: Step one: the 4 ppt PFOA/PFOS limits stand, monitoring is due in 2027 and compliance is proposed for 2031. Step two: treatment media saturates and must be replaced every one to three years. Step three: landfills increasingly refuse it, destruction capacity is thin, and utilities fear long-tail liability (PFOA and PFOS were designated CERCLA hazardous substances in 2024, from my background knowledge). The brief flags disposal as a downstream bottleneck but it is unverified.
solution: Start as a broker: aggregate small batches into full loads, match them to thermal reactivation, high-temperature incineration or newer destruction technologies, and issue a standard 'certificate of destruction' with custody records (tagged bulk bags, manifests, destruction-efficiency evidence and insurance). Sell it to media vendors as a bundled add-on. Later, add software for utilities' liability files.
why_now: Utilities that installed treatment after state limits and settlement money (3M and DuPont) are now hitting first change-outs. The delay from 2029 to 2031 moves the compliance date but not the disposal-liability clock.
revenue_model: 15-25% margin on disposal contracts ($ per ton), annual custody-software subscription and insurance-backed certificate fees.
non_obvious_insight: Regulatory relief changes when utilities must install treatment, not who owns the waste after it is installed. Buyers want absolution and paperwork more than the cheapest disposal, so documentation and insurance are the product.
first_30_days: Identify 10-20 utilities with early PFAS installs and imminent media change-outs from state announcements. Interview two disposal handlers and one reactivation vendor. Have an environmental attorney review a certificate template. Sign three pilot loads.

title: Neutral Legacy Animal-Data Vault for NAM Validation
one_liner: A neutral data trust that turns pharma's shelved animal-study results into blinded concordance benchmarks organoid and organ-chip makers use to prove their methods are 'adequately validated.'
customer: Organoid, organ-chip and other NAM startups needing FDA-credible validation, CROs, and pharma tox groups that contribute data and earn credits.
problem: FDA's Sept 21, 2026 direct final rule swapped 'animal tests' for 'nonclinical tests' but requires methods to be 'adequately validated'. Its NAM use-case database has only 25 entries. Validation needs ground truth: in vivo and clinical outcomes for many compounds. That lives in competing pharma archives and old PDFs, and pharma cannot pool proprietary data across competitors.
solution: Contributors deposit outcomes for shelved or dead compounds (species, dose, target-organ findings, human outcome where known) into a trust with blinded, query-only access. NAM developers submit predictions on a blinded panel of 100-200 compounds. They receive sensitivity, specificity and PPV by context of use, in a format built for FDA meetings. Contributors earn free validation credits. Start from public sources: FDA and EMA review documents, NTP, open toxicogenomics sets and DILI ranking lists.
why_now: The FDA rule landed this week and the NAM database is thin. NIH turbulence pushes toward cheaper methods. The IMI eTOX project pooled 8,196 studies on 1,947 compounds from 13 pharma companies, which proves the sharing model can work, but it was a research consortium and not a validation product.
revenue_model: $20-100k per validation report, annual memberships ($50-150k for NAM vendors; $100k or in-kind data for pharma), and licensing of benchmark panels to CROs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats animal data as obsolete. As new animal studies decline, the historical archive becomes a fixed, non-renewable supply and the only ground truth for validating replacements. Dead compounds carry no competitive risk, so the usual objection to sharing disappears. The owner of the concordance yardstick becomes a toll-taker on every NAM filing.
first_30_days: Assemble a public 150-compound reference set with animal and human outcomes. Sell 3-5 'pre-validation concordance reports' at $10-20k to organ-chip and organoid startups. Interview 5 pharma tox heads about pilot contributions of 20-50 shelved compounds each. Recruit a former FDA nonclinical reviewer as an advisor.

title: Certify Overseas Eldercare, Insure the Trip Home
one_liner: An independent audit standard, trial-stay program and medevac-backed membership for Americans moving parents into care in Mexico, the Philippines or Thailand.
customer: Adult children and spouses of middle-income seniors (assets $50-150k) who can't afford $6,300 a month in the US and can't get Medicaid. Elder-law and financial planners are the channel, and overseas operators buy audits.
problem: Assisted living and memory care abroad run $800-3,000 a month with 1:3 to 1:5 staffing claims, but there is no independent quality standard, Medicare doesn't work abroad, and families have no emergency evacuation or continuity-of-care plan. Trust, not price, blocks the market.
solution: US-run unannounced audits by bilingual RNs against a published rubric (staff ratios, medication safety, dementia protocols, fire, hospital proximity), with public scorecards. Add a 30-day trial-stay package, a membership bundling medevac and repatriation cover from a partner, US-physician telehealth oversight, and a family-visit travel budget.
why_now: The 2026 visa pause and TPS terminations closed the door on importing workers, and Wisconsin nursing homes wrote off apartments bought for overseas hires. Labor now moves the other way: patients go to the labor. Alongside the US costs ($114,975 a year for a nursing home, $74,400 for assisted living) and 90% occupancy, families are already exploring it.
revenue_model: Family-paid vetting and placement fee of $750-2,500 (families only, to avoid conflicts), $600-1,200 a year membership for evacuation cover and telehealth oversight, and separate operator-paid annual audit subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody thinks seniors will leave the US, but the buyer is a middle-income family choosing between $115k a year and a waitlist. The moat is a trusted third-party scorecard and a way home, the same trust layer that made medical tourism scalable.
first_30_days: Visit and score 10 facilities in one cluster (for example Lake Chapala/Guadalajara) with a nurse partner. Publish the rubric and first scorecards, pre-sell 30-day trial-stay packages to expat and retire-abroad groups, and sign a medevac partner.

title: Mod-Neutral Escrow for Reddit Swap Subs
one_liner: A roughly 2% escrow-and-reputation rail for r/hardwareswap-style trade communities that auto-writes verified trade counts, so buyers stop gambling on PayPal Goods & Services and mods stop refereeing scams.
customer: Buyers and sellers of $300-$5,000 used goods in Reddit trade subs (GPUs/RAM/SSDs, mechanical keyboards, watches, cameras, audio gear). Fee is split between both sides. Power traders and flippers are the first users because they feel chargeback pain most.
problem: Reddit's swap subs are unofficial high-ticket marketplaces run on mod-maintained 'confirmed trades' flair and PayPal G&S. Sellers get hit by chargebacks or 'not as described' reversals weeks later, even with signature confirmation. Buyers get hit by bogus-escrow scams and friends-and-family requests. Leaving for eBay costs about 13%, and PayPal G&S costs about 3.5% plus a fixed fee. Mods burn hours every week adjudicating disputes with no tooling. They also cannot endorse a paid vendor, because the Moderator Code of Conduct (Rule 5) bars compensation for moderation actions.
solution: Buyer funds are held through a licensed escrow partner. The seller ships with tracking, signature, and a serial-number photo checklist. Funds release after delivery plus a 72-hour inspection window. Disputes go to an evidence packet reviewed by a small paid panel of trusted high-volume traders. Every completed trade writes to a public read-only 'verified trades' API, plus a free Devvit flair-sync app any mod team can install to update trade counts automatically. Mods are never paid and the rail never touches moderation decisions.
why_now: The 2024-present global memory shortage has pushed RAM, SSD and GPU prices up several-fold, and a June 2026 class action alleges DRAM price fixing. That makes used-parts ticket sizes large enough that a 2% escrow fee is cheap insurance. Chargeback fraud on P2P payments is also a growing complaint among sellers.
revenue_model: 1.5-2.5% fee per side (undercutting PayPal G&S and eBay), optional insured-shipping add-on, and later a partner revenue share or float income on held funds. Enterprise-style deals with high-volume resellers who trade weekly.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is mod-trusted neutrality, not payments tech. Mods can't take money and won't bless a vendor who could be partial, so the winning rail is the one that is publicly documented, has zero mod financial relationship, and hands mods a free tool that deletes their number-one time sink (dispute refereeing and manual flair updates). Adoption is pulled by mod teams, not pushed by marketing. Serious traders also fear the 60-180 day chargeback tail more than the fee.
first_30_days: Sign with a licensed escrow or payments partner (an Escrow.com-style API, or Stripe Connect with held funds) so you avoid money-transmitter licensing. Start in one tight, high-ticket niche such as watches or keyboards rather than r/hardwareswap itself. Recruit 15 top-flair traders as design partners and waive fees on their first 30 trades. Build the Devvit flair-sync app and a public transparency page. Target about 200 escrowed trades at about $600 average, and track dispute rate and time-to-release as the proof points for mod teams.

title: Third-Party Maintenance for Orphaned Robots
one_liner: Like third-party server maintenance for IT, a spares-and-support contract for robots whose makers failed, were acquired or stopped supporting them.
customer: 3PLs, retailers, hospitals and factories running AMRs, storage systems and delivery robots that are out of warranty or whose vendors are gone, plus lenders and bankruptcy trustees holding stranded assets.
problem: Robotics funding is concentrating (Skild $14B, Physical Intelligence $11B, Figure $39B) while the long tail starves. Agility is pivoting toward wheels, and Serve's roughly $1.3k revenue per robot signals shakeout. Buyers can be left with multimillion-dollar fleets without updates or parts.
solution: Buy stranded inventory and spares from failed vendors, arrange source-code escrow or reverse-engineer key consumables, and offer annual per-robot support contracts with SLAs. Also sell certified refurbished units.
why_now: The 2025-26 funding boom is producing its first wave of failures and consolidation, while Amazon (1M+ robots, building its own robot factory) and Symbotic ($2.25B 2025 revenue) centralize the market. The orphan pool is growing now.
revenue_model: $1.5-4k per robot per year in support contracts, refurbished-unit sales, and escrow and trustee fees.
non_obvious_insight: In every hardware boom the durable second-derivative business is keeping the losers' machines running. Buyers pay to avoid stranded assets, and your spares moat grows with each vendor that fails.
first_30_days: Identify 3 wound-down or struggling robot vendors, get trustee quotes on inventory (often pennies on the dollar), and approach their 5 largest customers. Sign 2 support contracts and open a small depot near Memphis or the Inland Empire.

title: Heir-to-Own: Sibling Buyouts on Inherited Homes
one_liner: Help the sibling who wants to keep the family house buy out the others by assuming the parent's low-rate mortgage and financing the rest.
customer: Adult heirs inheriting a home worth $300K-$1.5M where at least one wants to keep it. Distribution runs through probate attorneys and mediators. Capital comes from credit unions and community lenders.
problem: The default assumption is that inherited homes get sold and split. The recurring fight is one heir wanting to keep the house while the others want cash. The keeper often can't qualify for a cash-out refinance, because the estate isn't closed, income is thin, or no cash is on hand, so the outcome is a forced sale, a partition suit or a family break.
solution: A platform that (1) gets a neutral valuation (AVM plus appraiser) and a transparent buyout formula, (2) generates a sibling agreement covering the buyout, occupancy and carrying costs, with attorney review, and (3) structures financing: assume or continue the parent's existing low-rate first mortgage, plus a second lien or HELOC from a partner lender, closing when the estate can convey. Start as a licensed mortgage broker packaging these deals.
why_now: A large share of US mortgages carry rates near 3-4%, so the parent's loan is now valuable. Federal rules (Garn-St Germain and the CFPB successor-in-interest rules) generally let heirs keep servicing on an inherited mortgage without triggering due-on-sale. Gen X stands to inherit about $14T in the next decade (Cerulli), and market rates make cash-out refinancing unattractive.
revenue_model: Origination or broker fees of 1-1.5%, a $500-$1,500 platform fee for valuation and agreement docs, and referral or spread income from the second-lien partner.
non_obvious_insight: Locked-in low-rate mortgages turned the inherited house from an asset to liquidate into cheap capital to keep. The estate industry still defaults to 'sell', and lenders have no way to underwrite an heir with equity but no cash.
first_30_days: Pick one state. Sign five probate attorneys and one credit union. Get an MLO license or a broker partner. Handle three cases manually. Publish a free sibling-buyout calculator for estate forums and Facebook groups as the lead magnet.

title: Shared Apprentice Pools for Office Work
one_liner: A group-training organisation (the Australian trades model) for white-collar work. It employs new grads, trains them to supervise AI output, and rotates them across several mid-size hosts that share the cost and get first pick.
customer: Mid-size (100-2,000 employee) accounting firms, insurance brokerages, property managers, logistics and healthcare-admin employers pay host fees. The new grads are W-2 employees of the pool.
problem: Each employer rationally stops hiring juniors because AI absorbs junior tasks and trained juniors get poached. Collectively that empties the 3-5-year-experience pipeline around 2029. Stanford finds 22-25-year-olds in exposed jobs 19% below trend, and 42% of recent grads are underemployed.
solution: The pool hires 25-40 juniors per cohort and gives 8 weeks of workflow-specific training (AI-assisted bookkeeping, claims triage, contract abstraction). It then places them 2-3 days a week across up to three hosts for $38-50/hr as supervised AI-assist analysts with QA metrics. Senior mentors get stipends, and hosts pay a fixed conversion fee at months 12-18. The pool handles payroll, insurance and HR.
why_now: The freeze is widening (Aug 2026 Stanford revision), and AI tools make a trained junior productive from week two. Employers are stuck in a prisoner's-dilemma on training. Pooled employment is a proven fix in Australian trades and in Germany's dual system.
revenue_model: Host fees at 25-35% gross margin, plus conversion fees of $8-15k per hire.
non_obvious_insight: The junior freeze is a coordination failure (a training externality), not a technology fact. Hosts are buying a cheap call option on the scarce 2029 mid-level hire, and pooling removes the poaching fear that blocks individual employers.
first_30_days: Pick one vertical with retiring owner-operators (independent insurance brokerages or small CPA firms). Sign 6 hosts at a pilot rate through a state society or trade association. Hire 10 grads via college career centres. Use a PEO for payroll so you build no HR infrastructure.

title: AI Shuttle Mediation for Estranged Families
one_liner: Each estranged party talks privately with an AI that drafts consensus 'bridge' statements and safe first-contact messages, leading to a human-mediated reunion within six weeks.
customer: Estranged adult children and parents (about a quarter of US adults report estrangement from a relative), paying $300-600 per participant, plus elder-law firms and hospital social workers paying $1-3k per reconnection case.
problem: Estrangement is common, painful and costly (unrepresented elders, contested estates), and the first contact is where reconciliation dies because neither side wants to go first. Coaches cost $150 an hour or more, and both parties rarely agree to therapy together.
solution: A structured program. A safety screen excludes abuse cases. Each party completes private AI-guided sessions to articulate needs and non-negotiables. A consensus engine produces candidate bridge statements that both sides rate independently. The first-contact letter or call is scripted and rehearsed in role-play. It ends with a human-mediated 90-minute conversation.
why_now: DeepMind's 2024 'Habermas Machine' showed LLM mediators can find statements groups prefer over human mediators. 2026 voice models handle emotionally sensitive role-play. Estrangement is now widely discussed, and aging and estate systems increasingly hit its costs.
revenue_model: Per-party program fee, B2B per-case fees from elder-law firms and hospitals, and success bonuses.
non_obvious_insight: Reconciliation fails on asymmetric readiness: one side is ready and the other is not. An AI that can shuttle privately with each side at zero social cost solves 'who goes first', which is the real blocker.
first_30_days: Partner with two family-therapist mediators. Recruit 20 pilot participants from estrangement support communities at $300 each. Measure first-contact and second-conversation rates, then approach five elder-law firms with the results.

title: Scam-Compound Geo-Intelligence for Compliance Teams
angle: Pairing 2: Space economy x Cybersecurity/identity fraud (scam networks)
one_liner: A monthly geospatial register of scam compounds, built from satellite imagery and RF data, that lets exchanges and banks flag payees and merchants with a physical nexus to them.
customer: Financial-crime investigators and sanctions teams at crypto exchanges, stablecoin off-ramps, OTC desks, Asian correspondent banks and payment processors. Secondary: anti-scam consortia (for example GASA members) and the US/UK scam-center task forces that agreed on 4 Sept 2026 to coordinate takedowns.
problem: Chainalysis puts 2025 scam revenue near $17B, with AI-enabled operations averaging $3.2M versus $719K, and US investment fraud alone hit $8.65B. On-chain tools label wallets but nobody maps the physical compounds (Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, now spreading) to counterparties. Compounds relocate after raids, and enforcement and sanctions need evidence of place, not just of transactions.
solution: A register of suspected compounds and displacement corridors built from optical and SAR change detection (perimeter walls, dormitory blocks, razor-wire, rooftop dish counts, nighttime lights) plus purchased RF-geolocation data on satellite-terminal uplinks, cross-referenced to corporate registries and Telegram guarantee marketplaces. Delivered as a risk API and CSV: 'this payee's declared address, IP cluster or KYC address is within X km of a flagged compound', with analyst-reviewed confidence tiers and evidence packets for suspicious-activity reports. Also a relocation forecast near border economic zones.
why_now: The US and UK agreed on 4 Sept 2026 to coordinate scam-center takedowns, and 2025 sanctions on the Prince Group showed enforcement appetite. Commercial revisit rates and cheap SAR now make monthly monitoring affordable. Reporting has documented satellite-internet terminals at compounds, giving them an RF and imagery signature.
revenue_model: $3-8K per compound-exposure assessment for investigations teams and $10-25K per month for the risk feed and API. Consortium data-sharing licences later.
non_obvious_insight: On-chain analytics see money but not place, and compounds are physically huge, slow to build and hard to hide, unlike wallets. They sit in a gap between defense-intel EO buyers and commercial AML, so no one serves them. Compliance teams need geographic-nexus evidence to justify de-risking specific corridors instead of blanket bans, and a place-based register gives regulators something to point to.
first_30_days: Validate signatures on known compounds (KK Park, Shwe Kokko, Sihanoukville, Golden Triangle zone) with Sentinel-1 and 2 plus $5-10K of commercial imagery credit. Publish a free 'Compound Atlas' of 30 sites with human-reviewed confidence tiers. Pitch 5 exchange investigations heads and one anti-scam NGO consortium, and sell 2-3 paid assessments.

title: Pet Sitters as Home-Energy Field Workforce
angle: Pairing 2: Energy transition & the grid x Pets & animal health
one_liner: A trained, insured network of pet sitters and dog walkers who already hold house keys and midday access, performing unlicensed home-energy tasks that stall electrification programs.
customer: VPP and DR aggregators, utility weatherization and heat pump programs, and home-battery/heat-pump installers that pay per completed visit ($40-90). Homeowners see it as free or discounted enrollment.
problem: Electricians are scarce (about 81,000 openings a year) and data centers pay 25-30% premiums, so home electrification loses labor. But many program stalls are not licensed work: 'customer must be home' no-shows, devices offline, thermostat and smart-plug swaps, filter changes, weatherstripping, photos for interconnection paperwork, and plug-in solar setup. Each one is a truck roll priced like an electrician's.
solution: Recruit and background-check pet sitters and walkers, insure them, and train them on about a dozen no-license tasks with guided QR workflows. Schedule tasks alongside pet visits, with the owner's explicit opt-in and strict limits (plug-in and low-voltage only, no panel work). Route orders from utilities, VPP operators and installers, and include placement of pet-zone sensors where relevant.
why_now: Data-center wage arbitrage is draining electricians (one report shows $20 to $35 an hour), 25C/25D subsidies ended so programs are cutting cost per home, and at least nine states have signed plug-in solar laws (around 1.2 kW, UL 3700 exists), which makes non-electrician installs legal and needed.
revenue_model: Per-visit fee billed to the program ($40-90) with 25-35% margin after sitter pay, training and certification fees, and a subscription for large programs that need a managed scheduling and QA layer.
non_obvious_insight: The energy transition's shortage is not just electricians. A large slice of tasks need access and trust rather than a license, and pet sitters uniquely hold both, visit on a schedule, and are a labor pool data centers cannot poach.
first_30_days: Pick one metro where a local sitter collective or Rover/Wag-heavy sitter community exists. Recruit and train 20 sitters on 5 tasks (thermostat, smart plug, offline-device reconnect, filter swap, plug-in solar setup). Sell a pilot at $60/visit to one co-op or heat-pump installer needing post-install commissioning and connectivity fixes. Confirm liability coverage before the first visit.

title: Chosen-Kin Circles for Solo Agers
one_liner: Mutual health-care-proxy circles of 3-4 unrelated solo agers with legal packets and a professional backstop, sold as estate planning but delivering belonging.
customer: Adults 55-75 with no spouse or nearby children ($1,200 setup plus $29 a month), referred by elder-law and estate attorneys, and later employers' pre-retirement benefits and health systems.
problem: Trend chain: fewer children and more one-person households (29% of US households), then the first large kinless retirement cohort (roughly one in five older adults is an 'elder orphan' or at risk of becoming one), then hospitals default to statutory next of kin who may not exist or be estranged, ethics reviews and expensive guardianships follow, and nobody shows up. Loneliness and a legal vacuum arrive together.
solution: Match 3-4 members by neighborhood and temperament. Each signs reciprocal state-specific health-care proxy, HIPAA release, POA, pet-care and funeral-wishes documents. The circle meets quarterly at a facilitated dinner to refresh documents and check in. A professional fiduciary is the backstop, and a 24/7 dispatcher runs the call tree when a member is hospitalized, with a wallet card and QR link hospitals can scan.
why_now: The 2024-27 'Peak 65' wave brings about 4 million Americans a year into retirement, including the largest kinless cohort yet. LLM-assisted drafting made state-specific legal packets cheap. Loneliness is now a WHO-measured health metric, so systems are receptive.
revenue_model: Setup fee plus subscription, referral fees from attorneys, and enterprise deals where hospitals or plans pay to reduce unrepresented-patient cases.
non_obvious_insight: People will not pay for friends but will pay for a health-care proxy. Sell the legal and logistics wrapper and let belonging be the by-product. The documents make the circle real, because someone has promised to show up.
first_30_days: Partner with two estate-planning attorneys in one metro. Host three 'Circle Nights' at $299 per person including the document packet, and capture 30 members. Contract a fiduciary for the backstop.
